images.title: Reverse, subtract, divide by 9
images.purpose: Shows that reversing 47 to 74 and subtracting gives 27, which is 9 times the digit difference 3.
images.composition: Two number cards at the top joined by a swap arrow, and the working centred below them.
images.exact_structure: Plain white background, generous empty margins, the main object large and centred. Top: two rounded cards side by side, the left with a teal (#0072B2) outline holding 47, the right with an amber (#E69F00) outline holding 74, joined by one curved grey double headed arrow. Below, centred: the line 74 − 47 = 27 in dark text. Below that, larger: 27 = 9 × 3 in dark text with the 3 in reddish purple (#CC79A7), and under the 3 the small note 7 − 4 = 3 in reddish purple. At the bottom, centred: 9(b − a) in dark text. Exactly 2 cards and 1 arrow.

images.takeaway: The difference is always 9 times the difference of the digits.
images.description: Shows that reversing 47 to 74 and subtracting gives 27, which is 9 times the digit difference 3.

image_decisions.why: One picture ties the example to the rule: the quotient is the digit difference.
